{{Quote|10,000 of these illegal grenades in the hands of ''BX droid commandos'' and there won't be a clone left breathing!|Marrt|<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" />}}
The '''FEX-M3 nerve gas grenade''' was an [[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] hand [[Grenade/Legends|grenade]] that contained the [[Death/Legends|deadly]] [[Fex-M3/Legends|FEX-M3 nerve gas]]. Manufactured by the [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Arms]] corporation, the grenade was one of Czerka's several types of [[chemical load grenade]]s filled with various chemical payloads. Production of FEX-M3 nerve gas grenades was banned by the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] around the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]; however, one [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Czerka factory|factory]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Belgaroth]] secretly produced a large shipment of grenades for the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the conflict. When intelligence of the factory's possible ties to their enemy reached the Republic, a four-[[Gender/Legends|man]] [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] team was dispatched to [[Mission to Belgaroth|investigate]]. During the course of the mission, three [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] were killed by a native [[droidbreaker]] creature, but the remaining clone, [[Clone Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Marrt]], was able to complete the mission. He destroyed the shipment, burned the factory, captured its head, [[Tarin (Human)|Tarin]], and retrieved important data records that helped expose two traitorous [[Senator/Legends|senators]] in the Republic's midst. The grenade was in use again by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], and it was employed by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].

==Description==
{{Quote|The ''FEX-M3 nerve gas'' did its w-work. The creature was ''dead'' before it h-hit the ground.|Marrt|<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" />}}
[[File:FEX-M3_grenade_detonated.jpg|thumb|left|140px|A detonated FEX-M3 nerve gas grenade]]
The FEX-M3 nerve [[Gas grenade/Legends|gas grenade]] was a<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" /> tiny<ref name="Arms and Equipment" /> [[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] hand [[Grenade/Legends|grenade]] filled with the [[Death/Legends|deadly]] [[Fex-M3/Legends|FEX-M3 nerve gas]],<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" /> a potent and volatile<ref name="Miniatures Battles" /> [[Color/Legends|yellow]]-colored<ref name="NEGTWT">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> gas that attacked the autonomic nervous system and the [[Brain/Legends|brain]] stem of most [[Species/Legends|species]], effectively shutting those systems down and incapacitating the victim. Although the gas achieved its greatest effect when inhaled, therefore making [[Breath mask/Legends|gas masks]] a means of partial protection, they were not enough, as a portion of the FEX-M3 nerve gas was also absorbed through the skin. The only way to completely protect an individual against the effects of the gas was to wear a full [[Environment suit/Legends|enviro-suit]].<ref name="Miniatures Battles" /> One of a line of specially made custom grenades called "[[chemical load grenade]]s," the FEX-M3 nerve gas grenade was produced by the [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Arms]] corporation, and, according to Czerka's trade agreements, it was clearly marked with labels describing its dangerous contents. Each FEX-M3 nerve gas grenade had a market cost of 1050 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="Arms and Equipment" />

The grenade itself had rounded curves and consisted of a top cylindrical section and a protruded conical handle, separated by a somewhat recessed middle section. A circular cavity was located at the very top of the grenade, and rectangular protrusions were visible at the sides. The top section and the handle were light gray in color, while the middle section was slightly darker.<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" /> The grenade weighed only 0.5 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]]<ref name="Arms and Equipment" /> and had a maximum throwing range of 20 [[Meter/Legends|meters]].<ref name="Range" /> When thrown, the weapon was held by its handle. The FEX-M3 nerve gas grenade could be detonated by a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] shot directed at it.<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" /> When detonated, the grenade released the FEX-M3 nerve gas<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" /> in aerosol form<ref name="Arms and Equipment" /> in a small radius. The cloud of gas dissipated after a brief period of time,<ref name="Miniatures Battles" /> but it was powerful enough to kill a [[droidbreaker]] creature in an instant and was deadly to [[Human/Legends|Humans]] as well.<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" /> Upon detonation, the shell of the gas grenade disintegrated, preventing it from being refilled and limiting the FEX-M3 grenade to be a one-time use weapon.<ref name="Arms and Equipment" />

==History==
{{Quote|FEX-M3 nerve gas grenade! The Senate ''banned'' production of these last ''year''!|Marrt|<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" />}}
The FEX-M3 nerve gas grenade was developed at some point before or early in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" /> and it was produced and filled with its contents at Czerka Arms' factories. The grenade saw prevalent military use,<ref name="Arms and Equipment" /> as it allowed military units to kill enemy troops without damaging structures.<ref name="NEGTWT" /> Due to its deadly effects, the grenade was subsequently banned by the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]].<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" /> However, during the first [[22 BBY/Legends|two]] [[21 BBY/Legends|years]] of the conflict<ref name="A Trooper's Tale date">In the framing story for ''[[A Trooper's Tale]]'', [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] appears in her original [[Clothing/Legends|costume]] from ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', indicating that the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] takes place prior to the episode "[[Heroes on Both Sides]]," in which she [https://web.archive.org/web/20110902130558/http://www.starwars.com/theclonewars/guide/episode310.html receives a new outfit] to signify the passage of [[Time/Legends|time]]. "Heroes on Both Sides" can be dated to [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]] since it occurs between two episodes, "[[ARC Troopers (episode)|ARC Troopers]]" and "[[Pursuit of Peace]]," that are also placed in 21 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]] by two other sources: {{FactFile2014|62|21 BBY 17-18|Defence of Kamino}} and {{FactFile2014|7|KAT 1-2|King Katuunko}}, respectively. Therefore, ''A Trooper's Tale'' must take place after the beginning of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], but no later than 21 BBY, the date of "Heroes on Both Sides."</ref>&mdash;a year after the official ban was issued&mdash;a [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]&ndash;affiliated [[Czerka factory|factory]] owned by Czerka and located on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Belgaroth]] made a deal with the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]], a member of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. The head of the factory, [[Tarin (Human)|Tarin]], promised [[Reep Tonith]], the Clan's representative, to produce 100,000 FEX-M3 nerve gas grenades for the Confederacy in exchange for a large monetary reward.<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" />

[[File:Marrt_grenades.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Sergeant Marrt finds a shipment of FEX-M3 grenades.]]
When the Republic received intelligence of Tarin's secret dealings with the Confederacy, it dispatched a [[Scout/Legends|scout]] team of four [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] led by [[Clone Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Marrt]] to investigate. The team made their way to the factory; once they reached it, Marrt ordered his men to remain in hiding nearby while he went inside alone. Meanwhile, Tonith arrived to pick up the cargo, but found that Tarin had not yet completed the order. Tarin asked for a twelve-[[Standard hour/Legends|hour]] delay to allow him to produce the required number of grenades, and Tonith grudgingly agreed. Their conversation was overheard by Marrt, who then inspected the completed part of the cargo and found the grenades. Taking one FEX-M3 nerve gas grenade as evidence, Marrt tried to return to his squad unnoticed, but was spotted by Tonith's [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]] escort. As battle [[Droid/Legends|droids]] opened fire, Marrt and his men retreated to a [[Swamp/Legends|swamp]]. Tarin let them escape, believing that they would certainly be killed by the droidbreaker creatures native to the swamps.<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" />

Certain that the FEX-M3 nerve gas grenades would give the Confederacy an upper hand in the war and would spell doom for the Republic's [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|clone army]], the four clone troopers tried to contact the Republic, but were unable to do so because of a dense fog surrounding the swamp. At that moment, they were attacked by a droidbreaker that started killing the clone troopers one by one. Eventually only [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] Marrt remained alive, and in a last desperate attempt to defeat the droidbreaker, he climbed a nearby [[Tree/Legends|tree]] and threw the FEX-M3 nerve gas grenade he had taken from the factory at the creature. The droidbreaker caught the grenade in its mouth, and Marrt opened fire with his [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]]. One shot hit the grenade, which detonated and released its FEX-M3 nerve gas, instantly killing the creature.<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" />

Determined to avenge the deaths of his comrades, Marrt returned to the factory, destroyed Tonith's droids, burned the facility, and destroyed the entire shipment of grenades, but not before retrieving Czerka's data records. Marrt received heavy injuries, but was able to capture Tarin, although Tonith escaped. The data records Marrt had retrieved exposed two Republic [[Senator/Legends|senators]] who had been profiting on deals with the Confederacy. Despite the ban on the production of FEX-M3 nerve grenades and the destruction of the Czerka facility,<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" /> the grenades were eventually once again widely available during the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] years later, and they were used on the battlefields by both sides of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="Miniatures Battles" /> The grenade continued to see use during the devastating [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] decades later.<ref name="Arms and Equipment" />

==Behind the scenes==
The FEX-M3 nerve gas grenade was first mentioned in the [[1991]] [[Star Wars Miniatures Battles (first edition)|supplement]] for [[West End Games]]' tabletop wargame system, ''[[Star Wars Miniatures Battles]]''. The grenades were presented as one of the several types of ordnance available for use during the game.<ref name="Miniatures Battles">[[Star Wars Miniatures Battles (first edition)|''Star Wars Miniatures Battles'', First Edition]]</ref> The grenade went unreferenced for many years until it was mentioned as one of the types of chemical load grenades in the [[2002]] ''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]'', a supplement for [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="Arms and Equipment" /> The grenade was later briefly referenced in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]'', a [[2004]] reference book,<ref name="NEGTWT" /> before making its first actual appearance in ''[[A Trooper's Tale]]'', a short [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] strip published in ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.8|Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic UK 6.8]]'' in [[May]] of [[2010]]. ''A Trooper's Tale'' was written by [[Robin Etherington]] and illustrated by [[Andres Ponce]].<ref name="A Trooper's Tale" />
